text:
B: Hi! Sorry, hi, can you hear me?
A: Yeah. Hi. Craig.
B: I'm Chloe. Erm, how are you?
A: Fine. Bit knackered. You?
B: Yeah, good, thanks. A bit nervous. I'm always nervous, don't worry, it's not you. Well, it might be a bit you. Sorry, that came out wrong.
A: It's fine.
B: ...So, erm, what do you do?
A: Software developer. Logistics stuff. You're at uni, yeah?
B: Yeah, how did you know?
A: Just a guess. Your room. The cork board.
B: Oh, God, yeah. That's all my placement timetables. I'm doing primary teaching, third year. Last placement soon, so I'm sort of living on that board at the minute.
A: Right. My mum was a school receptionist. Primary.
B: Oh, nice! They run the whole place, honestly. Our receptionist on my last placement knew every kid's name, every parent's name, who was allowed to pick up who. Without her the head would've just been stood in the corridor crying.
A: Yeah, that sounds like my mum.
B: What's it like, the software stuff? Sorry, I don't really know anything about it.
A: It's alright. I sit in a box room and fix things that other people broke. Pays well, so.
B: I bet. Teaching doesn't, really. Everyone keeps telling me that, like I don't know.
A: Why do it, then?
B: Erm. Because of the kids, I suppose. It sounds cheesy. But there was a little girl in my Year 4 class who wouldn't come in the door in the mornings, she'd just stand there holding her mum's coat. And by the end of the placement she'd come in and show me her reading book. That was kind of the best thing I've done, if that makes sense.
A: Yeah. Fair enough. That's more than I can say for my job.
B: Aw, no, I'm sure it's useful.
A: It's useful. It's not that.
B: Mm. Erm, are those gaming headphones?
A: Yeah. I play a lot. Probably too much.
B: My brother's the same, he's seventeen. He's up till about three and then my mum's shouting up the stairs. He's doing an electrical apprenticeship with my dad.
A: Electrician, your dad?
B: Yeah, self-employed.
A: Smart. They earn more than people think. Better than uni, half the time.
B: Oh. Yeah, maybe. I'm the first one in my family to go, so. Bit late now.
A: No, I didn't mean you. Mine was a waste of money 'cause I didn't turn up. A 2:2.
B: Oh, that's still good!
A: It's alright. Nobody's asked since.
B: Well, that's something. Erm, where are you based?
A: Stevenage.
B: Is that near London? Sorry, I'm terrible with—
